name: GetConsentio Cookie Banner – GDPR Cookie Consent
author: rovidevconsentio

sections.description:
Get a GDPR / ePrivacy cookie banner running on your WordPress site in two minutes, without slowing it down. GetConsentio loads a script of under 9 KB (gzipped) with defer, so your Core Web Vitals stay green, and it blocks analytics and advertising scripts until the visitor actually consents.

The plugin connects your site to the GetConsentio consent management service. Create a free site key, paste it under Settings → GetConsentio, and the banner is live. Full documentation: getconsentio.com/docs.

Why site owners choose GetConsentio

  • Prior consent that really works (opt-in). Optional auto-block holds back known trackers until the visitor accepts, so you are not just showing a banner while cookies are already set.
  • Google Consent Mode v2. All four signals (ad_storage, analytics_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization) are set before your Google tags fire. Google Consent Mode is a Google feature; this plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google.
  • EU opt-in and US opt-out. Choose GDPR (opt-in), US-style opt-out, or let the country decide automatically.
  • Fast. Under 9 KB gzipped, loaded with defer from a CDN. No jQuery, no extra render-blocking requests.
  • Speaks your visitors’ language. Spanish, English, French, German, Italian and Portuguese, detected automatically from the visitor’s language or country.
  • Proof of consent. Consent choices are logged in your GetConsentio dashboard, which is what regulators ask for when they ask for evidence.
  • Easy withdrawal of consent. A [consentio_preferences_link] shortcode adds a “Cookie settings” link anywhere.
  • Guided setup. A 3-step checklist on the settings screen, translated into Spanish, Italian, German, French and Portuguese.
  • Cookie declaration page. Add a live, always up to date cookie table to any page with the [consentio_cookie_declaration] shortcode.
  • Your look. Center or bottom position, light or dark theme, your accent color, your company name and cookie policy link.
  • Free plan available. Start for free; upgrade only if you need more sites or features.

Works with your stack

Standard WordPress script queue, so it works with any theme that calls wp_head(): Astra, GeneratePress, Divi, Elementor, Kadence, Block themes (Twenty Twenty-Five and newer), WooCommerce stores, and Site Kit / Google Analytics / Google Tag Manager / Meta Pixel setups. Add the banner once and it covers every page.

Who is it for?

Blogs, small businesses, agencies managing client sites, WooCommerce shops and any site in the EU, UK, Switzerland or with EU visitors that uses analytics, advertising or embedded media.

Not legal advice

A cookie banner helps with compliance but does not by itself make a site compliant. Review your cookie policy and privacy policy with a qualified adviser.

External services

This plugin connects to the Consentio consent management service (getconsentio.com) to display the cookie banner and record visitor consent. This is the same service the plugin is built for — it does not work without it.

  • What it is and what it’s used for: Consentio is a cookie consent banner (CMP) that shows visitors the consent choices, applies Google Consent Mode v2 signals, and (if enabled) blocks non-essential scripts until the visitor consents.
  • What data is sent and when: on every page load, the plugin loads a script from https://getconsentio.com/consentio.min.js, configured with the site key and settings you enter under Settings → GetConsentio (company name, cookie policy URL, region, language, position, theme, categories). Once the visitor makes a choice, that choice (and, depending on your plan, technical data such as IP-derived country and browser user agent) is sent to and stored by getconsentio.com to keep a record of consent, as required by GDPR/CCPA and similar laws.
  • Terms and privacy policy: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the getconsentio-cookie-banner folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it from Plugins → Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Create a free site key at getconsentio.com (about one minute).
  4. Go to Settings → GetConsentio, paste your site key and set company name, cookie policy URL, region, language, position, theme and color. Save.
  5. Open your site in a private window: the banner appears. Optional: add [consentio_cookie_declaration] to your cookie policy page.
sections.faq:
Do I need a GetConsentio account?

Yes. You need a site key (a free plan is available) so the banner can log consents. Creating it takes about a minute at getconsentio.com.

Is it GDPR compliant?

It implements prior consent (opt-in) with real script blocking, granular categories, easy withdrawal and a log of each consent. Compliance also depends on your cookie policy and how you configure your tags; this is not legal advice.

Does it support Google Consent Mode v2?

Yes, with all four consent signals, set before Google tags load. Required for Google Ads and GA4 audiences in the EEA.

Does it block Google Analytics, Meta Pixel and other trackers until consent?

Enable Auto-block in the settings and known trackers are held back until the visitor accepts the relevant category.

Will it slow down my site?

No. The script is under 9 KB gzipped, served from a CDN and loaded with defer.

Does it work with caching plugins (WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache)?

Yes. The banner runs in the browser, so page caching does not affect it. If your optimizer delays or combines JavaScript, exclude the consentio script from delay/minify so the banner loads before your analytics tags.

Does it work with WooCommerce, Elementor, Divi or Gutenberg?

Yes. It uses the standard WordPress script queue, so it works with any theme or page builder.

The banner does not show on my site. What should I check?

  1. Make sure you pasted the site key (it starts with cs_) under Settings → GetConsentio and saved.
  2. Open the site in a private window and clear your page cache / CDN cache.
  3. If you use an optimizer that delays or combines JavaScript, exclude the consentio script from it.
  4. The banner is intentionally not loaded inside the Customizer or page-builder editors; check the live site.

Can visitors change their choice later?

Yes. Add the [consentio_preferences_link] shortcode (for example in a footer widget or menu) to show a “Cookie settings” link that reopens the banner.

Can I show the cookie table on a page?

Yes. Use the [consentio_cookie_declaration] shortcode on any page or post.

Can I change the language or show it by country?

Yes. Choose a fixed language, the visitor’s browser language, or automatic by country.

What happens to my settings if I uninstall the plugin?

The plugin removes its saved settings on uninstall. Consent records stay in your GetConsentio account, where you can export them.

Where can I get help?

Use the support forum here, or write to hello@getconsentio.com.
sections.changelog:
1.3.0

  • New: Consent Mode v2 is set to “denied” at the very top of the page (GDPR region) so Google tags added by other plugins can never run before the default is in place.
  • New: guided setup on the settings screen (3 steps while no key is set, “Banner active” status once it is), and a redirect to the settings page right after activation.
  • New: [consentio_preferences_link] shortcode – a “Cookie settings” link visitors can use to change or withdraw consent at any time.
  • New: admin screen translated into Spanish, Italian, German, French and Portuguese.
  • New: the cookie policy link defaults to your WordPress privacy policy page when left empty.
  • New: native color picker for the accent color; the site key is validated and a clear message appears if it looks wrong.
  • Improved: the banner no longer loads inside the Customizer or the Elementor, Beaver Builder, Divi and Bricks editors.
  • Security: configuration JSON is now encoded with JSON_HEX_TAG / JSON_HEX_AMP.

1.2.4

  • Settings page: the “Enter your site key” notice now links straight to the free sign-up so you can get a key in about a minute.

1.2.3

  • Plugin name no longer includes third-party product names (“Consent Mode”), per the Plugin Directory naming guidelines. Google Consent Mode v2 is still supported; it is a Google feature and this plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google.
  • Readme: consistent settings page name (Settings → GetConsentio).

1.2.2

  • Fix: the banner script is now registered with a plain false (load in header) instead of an array argument that only WordPress 6.3+ understands, so it loads in the header on WordPress 5.8-6.2 as well (before it could end up in the footer there).

1.2.1

  • Settings screen strings translated from Spanish to English (source language), matching the readme and WordPress.org conventions.
  • Cookie declaration shortcode: the inline script that triggers Consentio.renderDeclaration() is now registered and enqueued via wp_register_script() / wp_add_inline_script() instead of being printed as a raw <script> tag in the shortcode output, and only loads on pages that actually use the shortcode.
  • Documented the plugin’s use of the Consentio external service (getconsentio.com) in this readme, with links to its Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

1.2.0

  • Script now registered and enqueued via wp_register_script() / wp_enqueue_script() instead of a raw echo, per WordPress coding standards.
  • Bumped “Tested up to” to the current WordPress version.

1.1.0

  • Direct “Settings” link from the plugins list and a notice when the site key is missing.
  • Script cache-busting by version (?v=).
  • Stricter sanitization and an uninstall.php to clean up the option on uninstall.

1.0.0

  • First release: settings (site key, company, policy, region, language, position, theme, color, categories and auto-block), cookie declaration shortcode, and early injection in wp_head.
